BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on the Seller's "efficiency note":** The Seller's package says [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to focus only on [OPEN] items. Nothing in our record shows that agreement, and the Seller cannot pre-clear terms for us. I have reviewed every item, including those marked [STANDARD]. Most of the [STANDARD] items depart from our playbook.

## A. Liability and recovery architecture

**1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m vs our 25% / AUD 6m.**
The Seller's figure is our conditional fallback. That fallback can be used only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. Push back to 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25,000, basket AUD 250,000, deductible-style recovery.**
Our position is de minimis AUD 5,000, basket AUD 50,000, and first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded. The Seller's version is about five times our de minimis and basket, and it converts the basket into a deductible, so the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of losses. This is a material departure. Reject it.

**3. General time limit (cl 12.3/13): 18 months vs our 24 months.**
18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Push back to 24 months after Completion.

**4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13).**
This is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general limits. Our playbook requires these categories to stay separate. Reject it.

**5. Fundamental/Title claims (stated proposal).**
The Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits. This directly contradicts our playbook, which requires a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. This is one of the most important points to hold.

**6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5): apply to "all Claims of any nature".**
Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. The Seller's drafting carves out nothing. Our position is that no one may waive this carve-out. Title should also be excluded from these provisions.

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

**7. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).**
Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, is the whole-data-room and deemed-disclosure approach our playbook rejects. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only. Reject 1.1 and 1.2 in full.

**8. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).**
The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. Combined with item 7, the Seller has built a double bar: data room disclosure plus a buyer-knowledge exclusion. Our playbook requires deletion of blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name specific seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**9. Disclosure Letter 1.4 (non-admission).**
The standard "no admission" wording is acceptable in principle. However, it should not be read to cut across our specific conditions, the Bluefen and Riverlark requirements, or the specific indemnities.

## C. Specific transaction issues

**10. Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; Disclosure Letter 2).**
The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treating consent as satisfied on delivery. The disclosure confirms that no final written consent is included and that the associated conditions in clause 11.3 have not been evidenced. Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue, which is a material customer. Our playbook requires effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. Make this a condition precedent.

**11. Riverlark (cl 2/7; Disclosure Letter 3).**
The Seller proposes a release after Completion. The facility of about AUD 3.2m is confirmed as unpaid, and no discharge of security is included. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Push back, and check the PPSR for registered security as part of this.

**12. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; Disclosure Letter 5).**
The DD-005 completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are excluded from the draft funds flow ("a matter for the Seller"), and the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. This is a silent exclusion. Our playbook requires either a specific line item or Seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must reflect this before Completion.

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; Disclosure Letter 4).**
The Seller limits its indemnity to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180,000 and calls this adequate. Our playbook requires a broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The DD-010 figure of AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way, and clause 7.3 of DD-004 makes transfer of project materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Require broader coverage, evidence of payment or cure, and a confirmatory assignment.

**14. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (cl 4.6/Schedule 6; Disclosure Letter 6).**
The Seller describes this as "not expected to be material". The record is that a download link went to an unintended external address, and an export of about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps) may be involved. Scope, access and notification requirements are unresolved. Our playbook requires log preservation, investigation and regular updates, and it assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. We should not accept the "not material" characterisation, and we should not assert a breach either. Recommend specialist privacy counsel review, given the personal information involved, and require an investigation scope and update timetable.

**15. Sandbar renewals (cl 4.6-type "ordinary course"; Disclosure Letter 8).**
The Seller calls three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 "ordinary-course operating costs". The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together. Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic debt classification or price deduction. Request the contracts and terms, and reject the "ordinary course" label until it is evidenced.

**16. Tax and IP (stated position).**
The Seller considers these settled under the general regime. Our playbook keeps them open and assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the "settled" characterisation, and keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms.

**17. Title (stated position; Disclosure Letter 10).**
The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of title. Our playbook treats DD-012 as an internal supplied source, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC company extracts, a PPSR search, and confirmation of share transfer and authority to sell.

**18. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (Disclosure Letter 7 and 9).**
The disclosure states that the lease imposes a notification obligation and the Mossvale provision restricts assignment, but neither document confirms whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. The playbook does not address these directly, so I cannot advise a specific position. Obtain the landlord and Mossvale positions in writing, and consider whether either consent should be a condition or a specific indemnity.

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright:**
- The 20% cap, 25% de minimis, AUD 250,000 deductible basket, and 18-month period. Restore our positions: 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5,000, AUD 50,000 first-dollar, and 24 months.
- Subjecting Title/capacity to general caps and time limits, and any general override of categories.
- Carving out nothing for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.
- Whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
- The Seller's characterisations of Tax/IP as settled and the Sandbar costs as ordinary course.
- Relying on DD-012 as proof of title.

**Require as conditions or specific terms:**
- Bluefen: effective consent with evidence of conditions met before Completion.
- Riverlark: current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- Employee bonuses: a specific funds flow line item or Seller funding, including on-costs.
- Ironquay: a broadened indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure, plus evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment.
- Export/privacy incident: log preservation, investigation, and regular updates, with privacy counsel review.
- Independent title evidence, and clarity on landlord and Mossvale consent.

**Escalation:** Any concession on the cap, time limit or basket requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. Nothing in the Seller's package has been authorised, so none of these points should be conceded in the mark-up or correspondence.

**Caveat:** This is a playbook-based review to support the deal team. It is not a substitute for advice from qualified NSW counsel, particularly on the privacy, PPSR and enforceability questions.
